easy: Having to do with the way of life, art, and beliefs of a group of people.

ex.en: We learned about Korean cultural traditions at school.
ex.ko: 우리는 학교에서 한국의 문화적 전통에 대해 배웠다.

easy: To make something new that did not exist before.

ex.en: Scientists developed a new robot that can climb stairs.
ex.ko: 과학자들은 계단을 오를 수 있는 새 로봇을 개발했다.

easy: To think up a plan or idea and work on it until it is ready.

ex.en: My team developed a plan to win the science fair.
ex.ko: 우리 팀은 과학 박람회에서 이기기 위한 계획을 세웠다.

easy: To slowly start to have a new habit, skill, or feeling.

ex.en: I developed a love for reading in second grade.
ex.ko: 나는 2학년 때 독서를 좋아하게 되었다.

easy: A person who steers a car, bus, or truck and makes it go.

ex.en: The bus driver waved at us every morning.
ex.ko: 버스 운전사 아저씨가 아침마다 우리에게 손을 흔들어 주셨다.

easy: A person who controls the horses that pull a wagon.

ex.en: The driver told the horses to walk slowly.
ex.ko: 마부는 말들에게 천천히 걸으라고 말했다.

easy: Being used or being here now, not new.

ex.en: We used the existing rules for the game.
ex.ko: 우리는 기존 규칙으로 게임을 했다.

easy: Real and here, not made up.

ex.en: Scientists study every existing kind of frog.
ex.ko: 과학자들은 현존하는 모든 종류의 개구리를 연구한다.

easy: To grow crops or raise animals as your job.

ex.en: My grandfather farms corn in Iowa.
ex.ko: 우리 할아버지는 아이오와에서 옥수수 농사를 지으신다.

easy: To grow plants on land so that people can eat them.

ex.en: They farm strawberries on the hill near our town.
ex.ko: 그들은 우리 마을 근처 언덕에서 딸기를 재배한다.

easy: To rub something with a rough metal tool to make it smooth.

ex.en: Mom filed my sharp fingernail so it would not scratch.
ex.ko: 엄마는 내 날카로운 손톱이 긁지 않도록 줄로 다듬어 주셨다.

easy: To walk in a line, one person after another.

ex.en: The students filed into the gym for the show.
ex.ko: 학생들은 공연을 보러 줄지어 체육관으로 들어갔다.

easy: To make something that is broken work again.

ex.en: Dad fixed the flat tire on my bike.
ex.ko: 아빠가 내 자전거의 펑크 난 타이어를 고쳐 주셨다.

easy: To attach something so it stays in place and does not move.

ex.en: Dad fixed the shelf to the wall with four screws.
ex.ko: 아빠는 선반을 나사 네 개로 벽에 고정하셨다.

easy: To move through the air, like a bird or an airplane.

ex.en: The geese fly south every fall.
ex.ko: 기러기들은 해마다 가을이면 남쪽으로 날아간다.

easy: To move very fast.

ex.en: The kids flew out the door when the bell rang.
ex.ko: 종이 울리자 아이들은 쏜살같이 문밖으로 나갔다.

easy: To control an airplane while it is in the sky.

ex.en: My uncle flies a small plane on weekends.
ex.ko: 삼촌은 주말마다 작은 비행기를 조종하신다.

easy: Saying exactly what you think, even if it is hard to hear.

ex.en: My coach was frank and said we needed more practice.
ex.ko: 우리 코치님은 솔직하게 더 연습해야 한다고 말씀하셨다.

easy: A person whose job is to show visitors around a place.

ex.en: The museum guide showed us the dinosaur bones.
ex.ko: 박물관 안내원이 우리에게 공룡 뼈를 보여 주었다.

easy: A person who leads you and shows you the way.

ex.en: Our guide led us up the mountain trail.
ex.ko: 우리 안내자가 산길을 따라 우리를 이끌었다.

easy: A book or paper that tells you about a place or how to do something.

ex.en: The park guide has a map and a list of animals.
ex.ko: 공원 안내서에는 지도와 동물 목록이 있다.

easy: A careful search to find out the truth about something wrong.

ex.en: Police began an investigation into who took the bike.
ex.ko: 경찰은 누가 자전거를 가져갔는지 조사를 시작했다.

easy: Careful work to find out all the facts about something.

ex.en: Our class did an investigation of how plants grow.
ex.ko: 우리 반은 식물이 어떻게 자라는지 조사했다.

easy: Giving you money for the work you do.

ex.en: My sister got a paying job at the ice cream shop.
ex.ko: 누나는 아이스크림 가게에서 돈을 받는 일자리를 얻었다.

easy: To make an amount bigger or higher.

ex.en: The shop raised the price of ice cream.
ex.ko: 가게가 아이스크림 가격을 올렸다.

easy: To move something up to a higher place.

ex.en: Raise your hand if you know the answer.
ex.ko: 답을 알면 손을 드세요.

easy: To move along by turning over and over.

ex.en: The ball rolled down the hill into the pond.
ex.ko: 공이 언덕 아래 연못으로 굴러 내려갔다.

easy: To move along on wheels.

ex.en: The skateboard rolled down the sidewalk.
ex.ko: 스케이트보드가 인도를 따라 굴러갔다.

easy: A little bit.

ex.en: My new shoes are slightly too big.
ex.ko: 새 신발이 약간 크다.

easy: To tell someone your idea about what to do.

ex.en: I suggested that we play tag at recess.
ex.ko: 나는 쉬는 시간에 술래잡기를 하자고 제안했다.

easy: To show that something might be true without saying it.

ex.en: Dark clouds suggest that it may rain soon.
ex.ko: 먹구름은 곧 비가 올지도 모른다는 것을 암시한다.

easy: To make you think of something.

ex.en: The smell of cookies suggests Grandma's kitchen.
ex.ko: 쿠키 냄새는 할머니의 부엌을 떠올리게 한다.

easy: The feeling you get when something happens that you did not expect.

ex.en: She jumped with surprise when everyone shouted "Happy birthday!"
ex.ko: 모두가 "생일 축하해!"라고 외치자 그녀는 깜짝 놀라 펄쩍 뛰었다.

easy: Something that happens when you did not expect it.

ex.en: The trip to the zoo was a surprise for the kids.
ex.ko: 동물원 여행은 아이들에게 깜짝 선물이었다.

easy: Having to do with machines or special skills.

ex.en: We had a technical problem, so the video would not play.
ex.ko: 기술적인 문제가 생겨서 영상이 재생되지 않았다.

easy: To use a special way to change something so it is ready or better.

ex.en: The factory treats the water so it is safe to drink.
ex.ko: 공장은 물을 마실 수 있도록 처리한다.

easy: To help a sick or hurt person get better.

ex.en: The nurse treated the cut on my knee.
ex.ko: 간호사 선생님이 내 무릎의 상처를 치료해 주셨다.

easy: Different from everything else; there is nothing else like it.

ex.en: Every snowflake is unique.
ex.ko: 눈송이는 저마다 독특하다.

easy: Found only in one place or one group.

ex.en: Kangaroos in the wild are unique to Australia.
ex.ko: 야생 캥거루는 호주에만 산다.

easy: The only one of its kind.

ex.en: My drawing of a purple dragon is unique in our class.
ex.ko: 보라색 용 그림은 우리 반에서 나만 그렸다.

easy: A group of many different kinds of things.

ex.en: The store has a variety of candy in big jars.
ex.ko: 그 가게에는 큰 병에 여러 가지 사탕이 들어 있다.

easy: Having many different kinds of things.

ex.en: Our school lunch has a lot of variety.
ex.ko: 우리 학교 급식은 매우 다양하다.

easy: Hurting people on purpose by hitting or fighting.

ex.en: Our school teaches kids to solve problems without violence.
ex.ko: 우리 학교는 폭력 없이 문제를 해결하라고 가르친다.

easy: Very strong, wild force.

ex.en: We were scared by the violence of the storm.
ex.ko: 우리는 폭풍의 거센 기세에 겁이 났다.

easy: A young person, like a teenager.

ex.en: A youth helped the old man carry his bags.
ex.ko: 한 청소년이 할아버지의 가방을 들어 주었다.

easy: All the young people as a group.

ex.en: The youth of our town cleaned the park.
ex.ko: 우리 마을 젊은이들이 공원을 청소했다.

easy: The years when you are growing up, after being a little kid.

ex.en: My grandpa played baseball in his youth.
ex.ko: 할아버지는 젊은 시절 야구를 하셨다.

easy: To feel thankful for something someone did for you.

ex.en: I appreciate your help with my homework.
ex.ko: 숙제를 도와줘서 고마워.

easy: To understand how important or true something is.

ex.en: Now I appreciate how hard Mom works.
ex.ko: 이제 엄마가 얼마나 힘들게 일하시는지 알겠다.

easy: To love something and think it is very special.

ex.en: I appreciate my old teddy bear because Grandma gave it to me.
ex.ko: 나는 할머니가 주신 선물이라서 낡은 곰 인형을 소중히 여긴다.

easy: When something comes apart into pieces.

ex.en: The breaking of the window made a loud crash.
ex.ko: 창문이 깨지면서 큰 소리가 났다.

easy: Not wet; with no water on it.

ex.en: Please give me a dry towel.
ex.ko: 마른 수건 좀 주세요.

easy: Not wet anymore and no longer sticky.

ex.en: Wait until the paint is dry before you touch it.
ex.ko: 만지기 전에 페인트가 마를 때까지 기다려.

easy: Very bad and wanting to hurt others.

ex.en: The evil witch in the story locked the princess in a tower.
ex.ko: 이야기 속 사악한 마녀가 공주를 탑에 가뒀다.

easy: Very happy and full of energy, so you cannot stay calm.

ex.en: The excited kids cheered when the team scored.
ex.ko: 신이 난 아이들은 팀이 점수를 내자 환호했다.

easy: For all time, never stopping.

ex.en: I will love my puppy forever.
ex.ko: 나는 내 강아지를 영원히 사랑할 거야.

easy: For a really, really long time.

ex.en: She took forever to get ready for school.
ex.ko: 그녀는 학교 갈 준비를 하는 데 엄청나게 오래 걸렸다.

easy: Money that is saved or ready to be used.

ex.en: Our class raised funds to buy books for the library.
ex.ko: 우리 반은 도서관에 책을 사 주려고 기금을 모았다.

easy: Damage to the body, like a cut or a broken bone.

ex.en: He had a knee injury and could not play soccer.
ex.ko: 그는 무릎을 다쳐서 축구를 할 수 없었다.

easy: An accident that hurts someone's body.

ex.en: The fall from the swing caused a bad injury.
ex.ko: 그네에서 떨어져 크게 다쳤다.

easy: A hard, strong gray metal that can rust.

ex.en: The old gate was made of iron and covered with rust.
ex.ko: 오래된 대문은 철로 되어 있었고 녹이 슬어 있었다.

easy: Very nice to look at or be around, so you feel warm inside.

ex.en: What a lovely garden full of flowers!
ex.ko: 꽃이 가득한 정말 아름다운 정원이네!

easy: So cute and sweet that you want to hug it.

ex.en: The lovely baby giggled at the puppy.
ex.ko: 사랑스러운 아기가 강아지를 보고 까르르 웃었다.

easy: Feeling angry.

ex.en: Dad was mad when I left my bike out in the rain.
ex.ko: 내가 자전거를 비 오는 밖에 두었더니 아빠가 화가 나셨다.

easy: A thin book with pictures and stories that comes out every week or month.

ex.en: I read a magazine about animals at the dentist.
ex.ko: 나는 치과에서 동물 잡지를 읽었다.

easy: A paper booklet with pictures and articles that you can hold.

ex.en: A pile of magazines fell off the table.
ex.ko: 잡지 더미가 탁자에서 떨어졌다.

easy: Made ready before it is needed.

ex.en: She read a prepared speech to the class.
ex.ko: 그녀는 미리 준비한 발표문을 반 친구들 앞에서 읽었다.

easy: Ready for something that may happen.

ex.en: We were prepared for the rain with umbrellas and boots.
ex.ko: 우리는 우산과 장화로 비에 대비했다.

easy: A few words that talk about someone or something.

ex.en: The teacher made a reference to our field trip.
ex.ko: 선생님은 우리 현장학습을 언급하셨다.

easy: A note that tells where you found your information.

ex.en: Write a reference for every book you use in your report.
ex.ko: 보고서에 쓴 책마다 출처를 적으세요.

easy: Something you use to find where you are or to compare things.

ex.en: The tall tree is a good reference point to find our tent.
ex.ko: 그 큰 나무는 우리 텐트를 찾을 좋은 기준점이다.

easy: In a place that you do not know exactly.

ex.en: My lost mitten is somewhere in the house.
ex.ko: 잃어버린 벙어리장갑이 집 어딘가에 있다.

easy: A net of many lines crossing each other.

ex.en: The cracks made a web across the ice.
ex.ko: 얼음 위에 금이 거미줄처럼 퍼졌다.

easy: A sticky net made by a spider to catch bugs.

ex.en: A fly got stuck in the spider's web.
ex.ko: 파리가 거미줄에 걸렸다.

easy: The part of your body between your shoulder and your hand.

ex.en: I hurt my arm when I fell off my bike.
ex.ko: 나는 자전거에서 떨어져 팔을 다쳤다.

easy: A website where a person writes about their life or ideas for others to read.

ex.en: My aunt writes a blog about her trips.
ex.ko: 이모는 여행에 관한 블로그를 쓴다.

easy: To write on a website where people share what they think.

ex.en: Dad likes to blog about his garden.
ex.ko: 아빠는 정원에 관해 블로그에 글 쓰는 것을 좋아하신다.

easy: The pitcher who comes in at the end of a game to help the team win.

ex.en: The closer struck out the last batter.
ex.ko: 마무리 투수가 마지막 타자를 삼진으로 잡았다.

easy: Nearer to something.

ex.en: Come closer so I can show you my drawing.
ex.ko: 더 가까이 와서 내 그림을 봐.

easy: Where everyone gets a fair say, like when people vote.

ex.en: Our class made a democratic choice by voting for a class pet.
ex.ko: 우리 반은 투표로 반려동물을 정하는 민주적인 결정을 했다.

easy: Words that tell what someone or something is like.

ex.en: She gave a description of her lost dog.
ex.ko: 그녀는 잃어버린 개의 생김새를 설명했다.

easy: Telling what something looks or feels like.

ex.en: His description of the cave made us all shiver.
ex.ko: 그가 동굴을 묘사하자 우리는 모두 몸을 떨었다.

easy: Very, very good.

ex.en: You did an excellent job on your science project.
ex.ko: 과학 프로젝트를 정말 훌륭하게 해냈구나.

easy: To be real and be in the world.

ex.en: Dinosaurs existed millions of years ago.
ex.ko: 공룡은 수백만 년 전에 존재했다.

easy: A person whose job is to watch and keep a place or person safe.

ex.en: The guard at the gate checked everyone's name.
ex.ko: 문을 지키는 경비원이 모두의 이름을 확인했다.

easy: Hooked together in a row.

ex.en: The joined train cars rolled slowly into the station.
ex.ko: 서로 이어진 기차 칸들이 천천히 역으로 들어왔다.

easy: Something you swallow or put on your body to feel better when you are sick.

ex.en: I take medicine when I have a cold.
ex.ko: 나는 감기에 걸리면 약을 먹는다.

easy: The study and work of helping sick people get well.

ex.en: My aunt studied medicine to become a doctor.
ex.ko: 이모는 의사가 되려고 의학을 공부했다.

easy: Being in a place; being there.

ex.en: The teacher noticed the presence of ants in our classroom.
ex.ko: 선생님은 교실에 개미가 있는 것을 알아채셨다.

easy: Being near someone, in the same place with them.

ex.en: I felt shy in the presence of the principal.
ex.ko: 나는 교장 선생님 앞에서 수줍음을 느꼈다.

easy: When two things mix and change into something new.

ex.en: Baking soda and vinegar have a fizzy reaction.
ex.ko: 베이킹소다와 식초는 거품이 나는 반응을 일으킨다.

easy: How you feel or what you do when something happens.

ex.en: Her reaction to the surprise party was a big smile.
ex.ko: 깜짝 파티에 그녀는 활짝 웃으며 반응했다.

easy: The language spoken in Spain, Mexico, and many other countries.

ex.en: My friend speaks Spanish at home.
ex.ko: 내 친구는 집에서 스페인어를 쓴다.

easy: The people who come from Spain.

ex.en: The Spanish are proud of their soccer teams.
ex.ko: 스페인 사람들은 자국의 축구팀을 자랑스러워한다.

easy: Having to do with Spain or its people.

ex.en: We ate Spanish rice for dinner.
ex.ko: 우리는 저녁으로 스페인식 쌀 요리를 먹었다.

easy: A game that people play using their bodies, like soccer.

ex.en: Soccer is my favorite sport.
ex.ko: 축구는 내가 제일 좋아하는 운동이다.

easy: Flat parts you walk up and down to go to a higher or lower floor.

ex.en: We sat on the steps in front of our house.
ex.ko: 우리는 집 앞 계단에 앉았다.

easy: The marks and path left by someone's feet as they walk.

ex.en: We followed the deer's steps through the snow.
ex.ko: 우리는 눈 속에 난 사슴의 발자취를 따라갔다.

easy: Saying one part of a word louder or stronger.

ex.en: In "banana" the stress is on the middle part.
ex.ko: "banana"에서는 가운데 부분에 강세가 있다.

easy: A tight, worried feeling when there is too much to handle.

ex.en: I felt stress before the big math test.
ex.ko: 큰 수학 시험 전에 스트레스를 받았다.

easy: Making something seem extra important.

ex.en: Our teacher puts stress on being kind.
ex.ko: 우리 선생님은 친절을 강조하신다.

easy: The way food feels on your tongue, like sweet or sour.

ex.en: I love the sweet taste of watermelon.
ex.ko: 나는 수박의 달콤한 맛이 좋다.

easy: What you like or enjoy.

ex.en: My taste in music is different from my dad's.
ex.ko: 내 음악 취향은 아빠와 다르다.

easy: A hot or cold drink made by soaking dried leaves in water.

ex.en: Grandma drinks green tea every morning.
ex.ko: 할머니는 매일 아침 녹차를 드신다.

easy: A bush whose leaves are dried to make a drink.

ex.en: A tea plant has small white flowers.
ex.ko: 차나무에는 작은 흰 꽃이 핀다.

easy: When you win a game or a contest.

ex.en: Our team celebrated its victory with pizza.
ex.ko: 우리 팀은 승리를 축하하며 피자를 먹었다.

easy: The part of the day after lunch and before dinner.

ex.en: We play outside every afternoon.
ex.ko: 우리는 매일 오후 밖에서 논다.

easy: A friendly hello you say after lunch time.

ex.en: "Good afternoon, class," said the teacher.
ex.ko: "여러분, 안녕하세요." 선생님이 말씀하셨다.

easy: A person who helps another person do their job.

ex.en: The vet's assistant held the kitten gently.
ex.ko: 수의사 선생님의 조수가 새끼 고양이를 살며시 안았다.

easy: Good for a very long time and loved by many people.

ex.en: Charlotte's Web is a classic book that parents loved as kids.
ex.ko: 《샬롯의 거미줄》은 부모님도 어릴 때 좋아했던 고전적인 책이다.

easy: A very, very good book, movie, or song that people love for many years.

ex.en: This movie is a classic that my parents loved too.
ex.ko: 이 영화는 우리 부모님도 좋아하셨던 명작이다.

easy: Things you wear on your body.

ex.en: I put on warm clothes before going out in the snow.
ex.ko: 나는 눈 속에 나가기 전에 따뜻한 옷을 입었다.

easy: Run by electricity.

ex.en: My dad's new car is electric, so it needs no gas.
ex.ko: 아빠의 새 차는 전기차라서 휘발유가 필요 없다.

easy: Not being able to do what you tried to do.

ex.en: His failure to catch the ball made him sad.
ex.ko: 공을 잡지 못한 일 때문에 그는 속상했다.

easy: Something that did not work out the way people hoped.

ex.en: The rainy picnic was a total failure.
ex.ko: 비 오는 소풍은 완전히 실패였다.

easy: Not getting what you were trying to get.

ex.en: Failure helps you learn what to do next time.
ex.ko: 실패는 다음에 무엇을 할지 배우게 해 준다.

easy: Smooth and even, not bumpy or tilted.

ex.en: Put the cake on a flat table.
ex.ko: 케이크를 평평한 탁자 위에 놓아라.

easy: Wide but not thick.

ex.en: I skipped a flat stone across the lake.
ex.ko: 나는 납작한 돌로 호수 위에 물수제비를 떴다.

easy: At the very start.

ex.en: My initial idea changed after I talked to my friends.
ex.ko: 내 처음 생각은 친구들과 이야기한 뒤 바뀌었다.

easy: The first letter of a name.

ex.en: The initial on my backpack is J, for Jun.
ex.ko: 내 책가방의 이니셜 J는 준을 뜻한다.

easy: To hit a ball or thing with your foot to make it go.

ex.en: She kicked the ball into the goal.
ex.ko: 그녀는 공을 골대 안으로 찼다.

easy: To move your legs and feet around in the air or water.

ex.en: The baby kicked her legs happily in the bath.
ex.ko: 아기가 욕조에서 신나게 발을 굴렀다.

easy: To hit someone or something with your foot.

ex.en: The boy kicked the tree and hurt his toe.
ex.ko: 그 아이는 나무를 발로 차서 발가락을 다쳤다.

easy: Letters and packages that the post office carries.

ex.en: The mail came early today.
ex.ko: 오늘은 우편물이 일찍 왔다.

easy: The way letters and packages are sent from place to place.

ex.en: I sent Grandma a card by mail.
ex.ko: 나는 할머니께 카드를 우편으로 보냈다.

easy: To get together in groups of two.

ex.en: Our teacher asked us to pair up for the science project.
ex.ko: 선생님은 과학 프로젝트를 위해 둘씩 짝을 지으라고 하셨다.

easy: To put two things together because they go well together.

ex.en: Pair each word with its picture.
ex.ko: 단어마다 알맞은 그림과 짝지어 보세요.
